criteria.rationale: Verified by probe: repository specs keep identical limits and problems, and preview and apply agree on an unsealed limit. The multi-line code span risk is stated truthfully in the spec. Unresolved parser assumptions are carried as low risks N12-N15, and the report wording as N16. The mutation claims of the execution log were not re-verified.
Parsing and admission logic only; no new shared state or lifecycle.
Refusals are bounded in number and size and keep their reason.
Refusal reasons survive the bound; the silent edge cases are the low risks N12-N14.

Compared base and new parser over every repository spec: no difference. A non-approving attestation with an open finding previews and records successfully. R6 is the declared API change and D1 keeps earlier run-backed records matching; parser behaviour changes on unusual Markdown are carried as N14 and N15.
Focused tests passed here; no probed case seals a cut limit.

Examined each change against its cause: run-length span reading for R2, a three-space fence bound for R3, a heading-as-written guard and quote-level truncation for R4, one shared unsealed-limit check in preflight and writer for R6, and the comparison-only legacy derivation of D1 for R8. The design delta reports no structural fact to map.

Read the manual wording changed in both locales and embedded copies against runtime behaviour: section and heading comment refusal and unterminated comment refusal hold, with the edge exceptions N12 and N15. The embedded copy differs from the root manual only by a block also absent from it at the base.
Examined refusal text: each probed refusal names the quoted line or limit and why, and the CLI preview and apply print the same blocker for an unsealed limit.
R1-R8 each have a passing test or the manual text; edge gaps in R1 and R3 are the low risks N12-N14.
Examined change set cs-0d82980be74c and the round 3 diff against R1-R8 and D1: each hunk serves a requirement or an earlier review finding and no non-goal is reopened.

Examined the limit authority boundary: probed comment and heading variants refuse rather than seal a cut limit, an unsealed limit is refused for every decision, and refusal echoes of the parser are bounded. N12-N14 seal nothing, which excludes nothing from review; N15 seals the text as written.

Compared with smaller alternatives: a local span scanner, two bounds, a one-condition guard and reuse of one admission helper, with no new dependency or extension point. A full Markdown parser would be the alternative if the recorded edge cases begin to matter; D1 stays valid while a later derivation changes only the sealed-limit check.

findings.action: Refuse such a heading, as the open spec follow-up states.
findings.rationale: Carries R1-N4: a heading "### Accepted --> limits", or a comment opened in the heading words and closed on the next line, yields no limits and no problem (R1 edge). No limit is sealed, so nothing is excluded from review.

findings.action: Count a tab to the next multiple of four, as the open spec follow-up states.
findings.rationale: Carries R1-N5: indent counts characters, so a tab-indented (or two spaces plus tab) backtick block opens a fence that silently hides a later accepted limits section.

findings.action: Read list-nested fences, covering the shallower closer, or record the changed answer as a decision.
findings.rationale: Carries R1-N6: a fence nested in a list item at four spaces is not read as a fence, so a comment opener in it refuses every limit. A further case of the same cause is silent: when such a fence is closed at two spaces, the closer opens a fence that hides the later section with no problem, where the base parser sealed L1.

findings.action: Report a fence line under a limit, or record the changed answer as a decision.
findings.rationale: Inside the section, a four-space fenced block under a limit is now sealed as flattened limit text with no problem; the base parser reported the fence and left the limit unsealed. Nothing is cut, but it departs from the rule in the parser comment and the manual that other content is reported, and no spec decision records it.
